policy_date: Dated 16 October 2021; effective from 1 November 2021 (lodged with ASX 2 November 2021)
covered_persons: All Directors and Group employees ('Employees'). A 'Restricted Persons' tier (Directors; senior management team as defined by the CEO; others who regularly possess inside information and have been advised by the Company Secretary) is subject to additional section 5 restrictions (blackouts, notification/approval, margin lending). Restricted Persons must also take steps in relation to dealings by persons over whom they have investment control or influence.
closed_periods: For Restricted Persons only: from close of trading on 30 June until and including the day of the ASX announcement of full-year results; from close of trading on 31 December until and including the day of the half-year results announcement; any other period the Board specifies. All Employees must also not deal when the Company notifies them not to (s 4.1).

derivatives.detail: No clause expressly addresses options, warrants or other derivatives. Touchpoints are the insider-trading description of 'deal' (entering an agreement to buy or sell, exercising options), forward contracts named as short-term dealings in s 4.2, and the broad hedging definition in s 4.3.
derivatives.evidence: buy or sell securities in a company, or enter in an agreement to buy or sell securities, or exercise options over securities, or otherwise apply for, acquire or dispose of securities (deal)

hedging_unvested.detail: Applies to all Employees. Securities acquired under a Company equity plan must never be hedged before vesting; hedging is any arrangement that limits the economic risk of holding Company securities.
hedging_unvested.evidence: Company securities acquired under an employee or director equity plan operated by the Company must never be hedged prior to vesting.

hedging_vested.detail: The hedging ban is confined to pre-vesting securities and securities under a holding lock or plan dealing restriction; vested, unlocked shares are not caught by s 4.3. A collar is an arrangement limiting economic risk and, on the s 3 'deal' description and the forward-contract example, likely a dealing: for Restricted Persons it is subject to blackouts, prior notification (Directors) or approval (other Restricted Persons), the 6-month short-term rule and the substance-over-form clause; other Employees are subject only to ss 4.1 and 4.2.
hedging_vested.evidence: Company securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee or director equity plan operated by the Company.

monetisation.detail: Forward sales, prepaid variable forwards and swaps are not expressly addressed. Forward contracts are named only as an example of a prohibited short-term dealing under the 6-month rule, and any structure that limits economic risk is hedging for s 4.3.
monetisation.evidence: entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts)

short_selling.detail: All Employees must not deal on a speculative basis, which expressly includes short selling.
short_selling.evidence: Employees must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short selling.

margin_lending.detail: Entering a margin lending arrangement over Company securities, or transferring Company securities into an existing margin loan account, requires prior approval via the s 5.5 written Clearance to Trade process. The Company may impose conditions, e.g. on when securities may be sold to meet a margin call. A disposal by a secured lender exercising its rights is an Excluded Dealing (s 6(e)).
margin_lending.evidence: Approval must be obtained in accordance with the procedure set out in section 5.5 for any: 1) entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities; and 2) transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account.

encumbrance.detail: No general prohibition on pledging or encumbering securities and no requirement that holdings be unencumbered; the policy addresses only margin lending (approval) and disposals by a secured lender (excluded dealing).
encumbrance.evidence: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

short_term_trading.detail: All Employees must not deal on a short-term basis, defined to include buying and selling on market within a 6 month period and other short-term dealings such as forward contracts. Selling shares received on vesting within 6 months of vesting is carved out.
short_term_trading.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 6 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

minimum_holding_period: 6 months in effect (buying and selling on market within 6 months is short-term trading); shares received on vesting may be sold within 6 months of vesting.

approval.approver: Directors: prior notification (not approval) to the Company Secretary and the Chair of the Board (Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee for the Chair). Restricted Persons other than Directors: prior approval via a Clearance to Trade Request Form to the Company Secretary; the policy refers to 'the approver' without naming the office. Margin lending (s 5.6) and exceptional-circumstances dealing (s 5.2) use the same s 5.5 process. Non-Restricted Employees: no clearance required.
approval.validity: Approval: dealing should occur within 5 business days following approval (or such other time specified), otherwise fresh approval is required; approval may be revoked at any time. Director notification: may deal for 5 business days following notification.
approval.post_trade_notification: Directors and other key management personnel must promptly notify the Company Secretary following any trade, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered into.
approval.evidence: you must complete a "Clearance to Trade Request Form" and submit it to the Company Secretary ... the approved dealing should occur within 5 business days following approval (or such other time specified in the approval), otherwise the approval is no longer effective

exceptional_circumstances.detail: A Restricted Person not in possession of inside information may apply to deal in a blackout period in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship or court-order compulsion) with sufficient evidence that the dealing is the most reasonable course of action.
exceptional_circumstances.evidence: Exceptional circumstances are likely to include severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order.

other_collar_relevant_clauses: s 1: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
s 2: Restricted Persons must also take steps in relation to dealings by persons over whom they have, or are deemed to have, investment control or influence.
s 4.3: Hedging is entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities.
s 5.3: By notifying their intention to deal, the Director is taken to have satisfied themselves that the proposed dealing is within the terms of this Securities Trading Policy.
s 5.5: the approver may impose conditions on the dealing in their discretion, is not obliged to provide reasons and may revoke their approval at any time.
s 5.6(b): margin lending approval may be conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, the circumstances in which securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
s 6(a): where plan securities cease to be held under the terms of that plan, any dealings in those securities must only occur in accordance with this Policy.

s 6(d): exclusion for trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan not entered or amended in a blackout, with no discretion and not cancellable in a blackout other than in exceptional circumstances.
s 6(e): exclusion for a disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example under a margin lending arrangement.
collar_assessment: A collar over vested shares no longer subject to a holding lock or plan restriction is not prohibited: the s 4.3 hedging ban is limited to pre-vesting securities and securities under a plan holding lock, and there is no derivatives, monetisation or general encumbrance prohibition. Given the 'deal' description, the forward-contract reference and the substance-over-form clause, the collar should be treated as a dealing: a Director must give prior notification to the Company Secretary and the Chair (or ARC Chair) and execute within 5 business days; a non-Director Restricted Person needs written clearance (5 business days, revocable, conditions may be imposed); execution must be outside the 30 June and 31 December blackouts and any Board-specified blackout, and the Director or KMP must notify the Company Secretary by close of business on trade date. A funded collar (loan secured over the shares) likely needs s 5.6 margin lending approval on a substance-over-form reading, and a collar with tenor under 6 months, or over shares bought on market within the last 6 months, risks the short-term dealing prohibition.
